The instant criminal misc. petition under Section 482 Cr.P.c. has been filed by the petitioner for quashing of FIR No.320/2022 registered at Police Station Bichhwal, District Bikaner and all consequential proceedings for offences under Sections 420, 406 and 120-B of IPC on the basis of compromise entered between the parties.

Counsel for the petitioners submits that the matter has already been compromised between the parties and it is borne out from the compromise that respondent No.2-complainant is not (2 of 2)
[CRLMP-1358/2023] inclined to proceed further in the matter.
Counsel has placed reliance on a decision of Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Anr. [(2012) 10 SCC 303].

sentences.text: In these circumstances, the impugned FIR and all consequential proceedings may be quashed on the basis of compromise.

Counsel for the respondent No.2 (complainant) concurs the fact of compromise and submits that in view of the compromise, the respondent No.2 (complainant) does not want to proceed further in the matter.

In these circumstances, the impugned FIR and all consequential proceedings may be quashed on the basis of compromise.
